title: Please sit here
scope: The infinitive and stem; commands for तू, तुम, आप (-ie, -iegā, irregular कीजिए, लीजिए, दीजिए, पीजिए, लो, दो) and the infinitive as a command; न and मत; से with कहना and पूछना; possession with का; को with indirect and specific direct objects; मुझे, उसे, उन्हें …

vocab.en: to him, to her (= उस को)

items.q: What is the stem of लिखना ?
wrong: लिखना is the infinitive itself. The stem is what is left when the ending -nā is removed.
लिखो is the तुम command, stem + -o.
items.why: The infinitive is the stem plus -nā: likh + nā.

items.q: What is the stem of सुनना ?
wrong: Only the ending -nā comes off. The stem keeps its own न, so it is सुन.
सुनो is the तुम command, stem + -o.
items.why: Remove -nā from सुनना and सुन is left.

items.q: Which infinitive does बैठिए come from?
wrong: Not a word. Take -ie off बैठिए to get the stem बैठ, then add -nā.
बैठ is the stem (and the तू command), not the infinitive.
items.why: Dictionaries list verbs by the infinitive, stem + -nā.

items.q: Which verb means “to bring”?
Which verb means “to call, invite”?
How is the infinitive ending -nā written?
items.a: Always as a full letter, never as a conjunct
wrong: As a conjunct when the stem ends in a consonant
The book stresses that -nā is always written with a full न, as in सुनना.
Dictionaries list verbs in the -nā form: बोलना, पढ़ना.
items.why: The infinitive is stem + -nā, with a full न.

lessons.title: बैठ, बैठो, बैठिए
lessons.desc: Commands for तू, तुम and आप

items.q: Fill the gap: “You read this letter. (to तुम)”
wrong: पढ़िए is the आप command. With तुम the command is stem + -o.
पढ़ alone is the तू command. With तुम the command is stem + -o.
items.why: Each pronoun has its own command: तू पढ़, तुम पढ़ो, आप पढ़िए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please come over here for a moment. (to आप)”
wrong: आओ is the तुम command. With आप the command is stem + -ie.
आ is the bare stem, the तू command, far too blunt with आप.
items.why: आप takes stem + -ie: आइए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You go quickly! (to तू)”
wrong: जाओ is the तुम command. With तू the command is the bare stem.
जाइए is the polite आप command. With तू the command is the bare stem.
items.why: The तू command is the stem alone. Its brevity shows intimacy or bluntness.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please have some daal. (to आप)”
wrong: खाओ is the तुम command. With आप the command is stem + -ie.
खा is the bare stem, the तू command.
items.why: खाना gives खाइए, the stem खा + -ie.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You close the window. (to तुम)”
wrong: कीजिए is the आप command of करना. With तुम the command is stem + -o.
कर is the bare stem, the तू command.
items.why: In बंद करना “to close” only करना changes; बंद stays as it is.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Children, you come quickly!”
wrong: आ is the तू command, for one person you are very close to. तुम लोग takes आओ.
आइए is the आप command. With तुम the command is stem + -o.
items.why: तुम लोग takes the तुम command, stem + -o.

items.q: Which is the extra-polite form of पढ़िए ?
wrong: -gā is added only to the आप command: paṛhie + gā.
The infinitive पढ़ना can be a command, but it lacks the deference of the आप form.
items.why: Adding -gā to the आप command makes it extra polite: “please be so kind as to read”.

items.q: Turn this तुम command into an आप command
wrong: लाओ is the तुम form. With आप the command is stem + -ie.
ला is the bare stem, the तू command.
items.why: आप takes stem + -ie: लाइए.

items.q: What kind of command is this?
items.a: An infinitive used as a command, to be carried out later
wrong: The तू command would be the bare stem पढ़. Here the infinitive पढ़ना is used.
That would be पढ़िएगा. The infinitive lacks the deference of the आप command.
items.why: The infinitive often gives a “deferred” command, and is most at home where तुम would be used.

items.q: How do you politely attract someone's attention, like “excuse me”?
wrong: सुन is the blunt तू command.
सुनो is the familiar तुम command, not the polite one.
items.why: सुनिए “please listen” is the polite way to attract attention.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please take this book. (to आप)”
wrong: Not a word: लेना is irregular, and its आप command is लीजिए.
लो is the तुम command of लेना.
items.why: Four verbs have irregular आप commands: कीजिए, लीजिए, दीजिए, पीजिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You give him this fruit. (to तुम)”
items.en: You[0] give[4] him[1] this[2] fruit[3]. (to तुम)
wrong: Not a word: देना is irregular in the तुम command too, which is दो.
दीजिए is the आप command. With तुम it is दो.
items.why: देना and लेना have irregular तुम commands: दो and लो.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please give Sita this bag. (to आप)”
items.say: आप सीता को यह थैला दीजिए ।
wrong: Not a word: देना is irregular, and its आप command is दीजिए.
दो is the तुम command. With आप it is दीजिए.
items.why: देना gives the irregular आप command दीजिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please rest. (to आप)”
wrong: करो is the तुम command. आप takes the irregular कीजिए.
कर is the bare stem, the तू command.
items.why: आराम करना “to rest”: करना has the irregular आप command कीजिए.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please smoke outside. (to आप)”
wrong: Not a word: पीना is irregular, and its आप command is पीजिए.
items.why: पीना “to drink; to smoke” gives the irregular आप command पीजिए.

items.q: Which four verbs have irregular आप commands?
wrong: आना and जाना are regular: आइए, जाइए.
items.why: करना कीजिए, लेना लीजिए, देना दीजिए, पीना पीजिए.

items.q: What are the तुम commands of लेना and देना ?
wrong: Not words: these two verbs are irregular, giving लो and दो.
ले and दे are the bare stems, the तू commands.
items.why: लेना and देना are irregular in the तुम command: लो, दो.

items.q: Turn this आप command into a तुम command
wrong: पीजिए is the आप command. With तुम it is पियो.
पी is the bare stem, the तू command.
items.why: पीना gives पियो in the तुम command.
items.en: You[0] have[3] some cold[1] coffee[2]. (to तुम)

lessons.title: मत, न, से कहना
lessons.desc: Negative commands; से and को with verbs of telling

items.q: Fill the gap: “Children, don't sit on that bed!”
items.say: बच्चो, उस पलंग पर मत बैठो !
items.en: Children[0], don't[4] sit[5] on[3] that[1] bed[2]!
wrong: The book makes commands negative with न or मत, not नहीं.
क्या asks a question. It cannot make a command negative.
items.why: मत (or the milder न) before the verb makes a command negative.

items.q: Which word gives the more forceful “don't”?
wrong: न also makes a command negative, but it is the milder word.
The book makes commands negative with न or मत, not नहीं.
items.why: The negative for commands is न or, more forcefully, मत.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Ask that washerman where my kurta is. (to तुम)”
items.hi: उस धोबी ___ पूछो कि मेरा कुरता कहाँ है ।
items.say: उस धोबी से पूछो कि मेरा कुरता कहाँ है ।
items.en: Ask[2+3] that[0] washerman[1] where[7] my[5] kurta[6] is[8]. (to तुम)
wrong: पूछना marks the person asked with से, not को.
पर means “on”. The person asked takes से.
items.why: पूछना “to ask” and कहना “to say” mark the person addressed with से.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Tell that servant that the room is dirty. (to तुम)”
items.hi: उस नौकर ___ कहो कि कमरा गंदा है ।
items.say: उस नौकर से कहो कि कमरा गंदा है ।
items.en: Tell[2+3] that[0] servant[1] that[4] the room[5] is[7] dirty[6]. (to तुम)
wrong: कहना marks the person told with से, not को. (बताना “to tell” does take को.)
items.why: कहना “to say (to)” takes से for the person addressed.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Tell Papa where the car is. (to तुम)”
items.hi: पापा ___ बताओ कि गाड़ी कहाँ है ।
items.say: पापा को बताओ कि गाड़ी कहाँ है ।
items.en: Tell[1+2] Papa[0] where[5] the car[4] is[6]. (to तुम)
wrong: से goes with कहना and पूछना. बताना “to tell” marks the person with को.
items.why: बताना takes को for the person told, the indirect object.

items.q: Make this command negative
wrong: The book makes commands negative with न or मत, not नहीं.
खाइए is the आप command. With तुम keep खाओ.
items.why: मत (or न) goes just before the verb.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please don't go there. (to आप)”
wrong: The book makes commands negative with न or मत, not नहीं.
क्या asks a question. It cannot make a command negative.
items.why: न before the verb is the milder “don't”; मत would also be correct.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This is Raj's bag.”
wrong: की is feminine. थैला is masculine.
के is plural or oblique. थैला here is singular and direct.
items.why: का agrees with the thing possessed, थैला, not with Raj.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where is Sita's bicycle?”
wrong: का is masculine. साइकिल is feminine.
के is masculine plural or oblique. साइकिल is feminine.
items.why: With a feminine thing possessed, का becomes की.

items.q: Fill the gap: “These are Mohan's toys.”
wrong: का is singular. खिलौने is plural.
की is feminine. खिलौना is masculine.
items.why: With a masculine plural thing possessed, का becomes के.

items.q: Fill the gap: “That boy's horse is very big.”
items.hi: उस ___ का घोड़ा बहुत बड़ा है ।
items.say: उस लड़के का घोड़ा बहुत बड़ा है ।
items.en: That[0] boy's[1+2] horse[3] is[6] very[4] big[5].
wrong: का is a postposition, so the owner is oblique: लड़के.
लड़कों is plural, “boys'”. उस is singular.
items.why: Being a postposition, का needs the oblique case before it.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where are these children's toys?”
items.say: इन बच्चों के खिलौने कहाँ हैं ?
wrong: बच्चे is the oblique singular (or direct plural). इन is plural, so the oblique plural is needed.
बच्चो is the vocative, for calling out to children.
items.why: The owner before का is oblique: बच्चों.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My glasses are in Brother's room.”
items.hi: मेरा चश्मा भैया ___ कमरे में है ।
items.say: मेरा चश्मा भैया के कमरे में है ।
items.en: My[0] glasses[1] are[6] in[5] Brother's[2+3] room[4].
wrong: कमरा is oblique before में (कमरे), so का becomes के too.
की is feminine. कमरा is masculine.
items.why: When the thing possessed is oblique, का becomes के.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My brother-in-law's car is new. (a woman speaking)”
items.say: मेरे देवर की गाड़ी नई है ।
items.en: My[0] brother-in-law's[1+2] car[3] is[5] new[4]. (a woman speaking)
wrong: देवर is oblique because की follows it, so मेरा becomes मेरे.
मेरी would agree with गाड़ी, but “my” goes with देवर.
items.why: मेरा agrees with देवर, which is oblique before की, although देवर itself does not change.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This is his dog.”
wrong: उसकी is feminine. कुत्ता is masculine.
का needs the oblique: वह becomes उस, written उसका.
items.why: उसका “his, her” agrees with the thing possessed, like any का.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Whose book is this?”
wrong: किसका is masculine. किताब is feminine.
कौन becomes किस before a postposition, written किसकी.
items.why: किसका “whose?” agrees with the thing possessed.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan and Sita are here, but their children are out.”
items.hi: मोहन और सीता यहाँ हैं, पर ___ बच्चे बाहर हैं ।
items.say: मोहन और सीता यहाँ हैं, पर उनके बच्चे बाहर हैं ।
items.en: Mohan[0] and[1] Sita[2] are[4] here[3], but[5] their[6] children[7] are[9] out[8].
wrong: उनका is singular. बच्चे is plural.
उसके is “his, her”, for one person. Mohan and Sita are two.
items.why: उनका “their” agrees with बच्चे, masculine plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where is Mohan's friend's car?”
items.hi: मोहन ___ दोस्त की गाड़ी कहाँ है ?
items.say: मोहन के दोस्त की गाड़ी कहाँ है ?
wrong: दोस्त is oblique because की follows it, so Mohan's का becomes के.
की would agree with गाड़ी. The first का belongs to दोस्त.
items.why: In a chain each का agrees with the next noun, and a noun before a postposition is oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This is the servants' room.”
wrong: नौकर का would be “the servant's”, one servant.
Not a word: the oblique plural of नौकर is नौकरों.
items.why: The owner before का is oblique, here plural: नौकरों.

lessons.title: को, मुझे, उसे
lessons.desc: को with objects, and the short pronoun forms

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please give this newspaper to Papa. (to आप)”
items.say: आप पापा को यह अख़बार दीजिए ।
items.en: {Please give}[0+5] this[3] newspaper[4] to[2] Papa[1]. (to आप)
wrong: देना marks the person given to with को, not से.
items.why: The indirect object, the person something is given to, takes को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You give me that kurta. (to तुम)”
items.en: You[0] give[4] me[1] that[2] kurta[3]. (to तुम)
wrong: मैं is the direct form. “To me” is मुझे (= मुझ को).
items.why: मुझे is the short form of मुझ को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please serve these girls samosas. (to आप)”
items.say: आप इन लड़कियों को समोसे खिलाइए ।
wrong: खिलाना marks the person fed with को.
के would make “the girls' samosas”, and leave no one being served.
items.why: With खिलाना “to give to eat” the person served is the indirect object, with को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “She doesn't like this kurta.”
items.say: उसे यह कुरता पसंद नहीं है ।
wrong: वह is direct. With पसंद the person takes को, so उस को or उसे.
items.why: उसे is the short form of उस को.

items.q: Which is another way of writing उन को ?
wrong: The short form has a nasal: उन्हें.
items.why: Oblique pronoun + को has a short form: उन को = उन्हें.

items.q: Which pronoun has no short form with को ?
wrong: तुम को has the short form तुम्हें.
हम को has the short form हमें.
items.why: आप को has no alternative form.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You call that servant. (to तुम)”
wrong: बुलाना takes the person called as a direct object, marked with को.
items.why: People as direct objects nearly always take को.

items.q: Why does कुत्ते have को here?
items.a: The object is one particular animal, so को marks it
wrong: से is not used here. को marks a specific direct object.
With a direct object को is not translated. It marks the object as specific.
items.why: को marks a specific direct object, much like “the” in English.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Don't you bring him here!”
wrong: वह is the subject form. The person brought is the object, with को, so उसे.
items.why: A person as object takes को, and उसे is short for उस को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please give these people water. (to आप)”
wrong: ये is direct. The person given to takes को, so इन को or इन्हें.
items.why: इन्हें is the short form of इन को.

wrong: बैठो is the तुम command. आप takes बैठिए.
बग़ीचा is direct. Before में it is oblique: बग़ीचे.

items.en: You[0] give[4] the money[3] to[2] Mohan[1]. (to तुम)
wrong: दीजिए is the आप command. तुम takes दो.
देना marks the person given to with को.

items.en: Don't[3] you[0] take[4] my[1] book[2]! (to तू)
wrong: लो is the तुम command. तू takes the bare stem ले.
The book makes commands negative with न or मत, not नहीं.
का is masculine. बहिन is feminine.
के is plural or oblique. बहिन is feminine singular.
लड़के is the oblique singular. उन and “boys'” need लड़कों.
कुत्ते is plural, so का becomes के.
मैं is direct. “To me” is मुझे.
दो is the तुम command. आप takes दीजिए.

items.en: {Please ask}[0+3] the servant[1+2] where[6] the milk[5] is[7]. (to आप)
wrong: पूछना marks the person asked with से.
items.order: After कि the question keeps its own order: दूध कहाँ है ?

wrong: Before को the oblique plural is needed: बच्चों.
जगाइए is the आप command. तुम takes जगाओ.
किसकी is feminine. थैला is masculine.
कौन becomes किस before का, written किसका.

items.en: {Please tell}[0+3] Mother[1+2] that[4] the tea[5] is[7] ready[6]. (to आप)
wrong: बताना marks the person told with को. से goes with कहना and पूछना.
चाय is singular, so the verb is है.
की is feminine. कुत्ता is masculine.
काली is feminine. कुत्ता is masculine.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: There is no नहीं, so the sentence is positive.
उन्हें is उन को, “to them”. “We” would be हमें.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: Raj, come over here a moment.
wrong: Raj, go over there a moment.
इधर is “here” and आओ is “come”. “Go over there” would be उधर जाओ.
There is no मत or न, so the command is positive.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: उसे बताइए कि नौकर बीमार है ।
items.a: Please tell him that the servant is ill.
wrong: Please ask him whether the servant is ill.
“Ask” is पूछना, with से. बताइए is “please tell”.
Please tell the servant that he is ill.
उसे is the person told. नौकर is the one who is ill.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: Brother, give the dog something to eat.
wrong: “Eat” would be खाओ. खिलाओ is “give to eat”.
There is no मत or न, so the command is positive.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: आप ये फल रसोईघर में रखिए ।
items.a: Please put these fruits in the kitchen.
wrong: Please bring these fruits from the kitchen.
रखना is “to put, keep”, and में is “in”. “Bring from” would be से लाइए.
Please eat these fruits in the kitchen.
“Eat” would be खाइए. रखिए is “please put”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: That would be बाहर कौन है ? किसका asks about the owner.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: That would be क्या यह आपका कुरता है ?

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: There is no मत or न, so the command is positive.
कल means “yesterday” or “tomorrow”. A command can only look ahead, so it is “tomorrow”.

items.q: Which form is the most polite?
wrong: बैठिए is the ordinary polite आप command. Adding -gā makes it extra polite.
बैठो is the familiar तुम command.
items.why: The ending -iegā is an extra-polite variant of the आप command.

items.q: Which postposition do कहना and पूछना use for the person addressed?
wrong: को goes with बताना and देना. कहना and पूछना take से.
items.why: माँ से पूछो “ask Mother”; उस से कहो “tell him”.

items.q: What does the bare-stem तू command suggest?
wrong: Respect is shown by the आप command, in -ie or -iegā.
That is the infinitive used as a command.
items.why: The तू command is the stem alone; its brevity accentuates its lack of formality.

items.q: When does a direct object usually take को ?
items.a: When it is specific, and nearly always when it is a person
wrong: A generic object takes no को, as in फल लाओ “bring some fruit”.
को also marks a specific direct object, as in उस नौकर को बुलाओ.
items.why: को marks a specific direct object, often like English “the”.

items.q: When the thing possessed is oblique, का becomes …
wrong: की is only for feminine things possessed, and does not change.
का stays only when the thing possessed is masculine singular and direct.
items.why: का agrees with the thing possessed in gender, number and case.

items.q: Which word means “which?” and agrees like an -ā adjective?
wrong: कौन means “who?” and does not agree.
items.why: कौनसा, कौनसी, कौनसे “which?” agree with their noun.
